summary:
Every rating is reading from the same hymn sheet right now, and that's the story of the day. R1 through R4 are all 6-1 (86%) on trends, sp, and hitting over the last 14 days, with sp riding a 3-game win streak across the board. That's not noise — four independent ratings converging on identical hot categories at identical sample sizes means the signal is structural, not a fluke in one model's weighting. The flip side is just as uniform: bullpen_fatigue is ice cold everywhere, 2-5 (29%) with a 5-game losing streak on all four ratings. If today's slate has a play that leans on bullpen_fatigue as a primary category, fade it or at least downweight it hard — this category has been bleeding for two weeks straight with zero divergence among ratings.

On today's board, prioritize games where trends+sp or trends+runs are both lit up — those combos carry the best season-long hit rates (58.0% and 57.3% at n=638/705) and now have the added tailwind of the hot 14-day run. R2 is the rating to lean on when strong plays line up: it's 4-1 (+3.0u) over the last 14 days and 9-4 (+5.0u) over 30, the best recent unit return of the group, while R4's strong-play sample has cooled to 50% (+0.0u) over 30 days despite a gaudy 64% season mark — don't let that season number fool you into overconfidence on R4 strong plays right now. Team-wise, if MIL, TBR, BOS, or LAD show up as the model's pick today, lean in — all four are running 69%+ win rates when picked, and BOS/LAD strong plays are hitting 76-80% with real unit profit (+19.0u, +27.0u). NYY is the one name to treat skeptically: 49% straight and -4.0u on strong plays, the only team near .500 at real volume, so a model pick on NYY today needs extra category confirmation before you trust it.
